---
title: pyplatypus
---

The engine behind [platypus](https://maju116.github.io/platypus/): semantic segmentation
and object detection in PyTorch, described by one specification and run from it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Working in R?

Read [the R package's documentation](https://maju116.github.io/platypus/) instead. It is
the same engine with an R surface on top, and its pages are written for that - it installs
this package for you and you never import it.
:::

## A run, in five lines

```python
import pyplatypus

spec = pyplatypus.from_yaml("run.yaml")
engine = pyplatypus.build_engine(spec)
engine.fit()
engine.evaluate("validation")
```

`from_yaml` and [`from_dict`](reference/from_dict.qmd) build the same object, so a
specification written by hand and one read from a file are the same thing.
[`build_engine`](reference/build_engine.qmd) returns the engine the specification's `task`
asks for.

## The same run as a configuration file

```yaml
task: semantic_segmentation
data:
  train_path: train/
  validation_path: valid/
  colormap: [[0, 0, 0], [255, 255, 255]]
models:
  - name: unet
    architecture: u_net
    input_shape: [256, 256]
    loss: {name: dice}
    metrics: [{name: iou}]
```

Everything not written down has a default, and the defaults live here rather than in the
caller - so a short configuration is a complete one.

## Where to start reading

| If you want to | Read |
|---|---|
| see every field a configuration accepts | [`spec_schema`](reference/spec_schema.qmd), and the field descriptions it carries |
| train and score something | [`Engine.fit`](reference/Engine.fit.qmd), [`Engine.evaluate`](reference/Engine.evaluate.qmd), [`Engine.evaluate_cases`](reference/Engine.evaluate_cases.qmd) |
| detect objects rather than segment | [`DetectionEngine`](reference/DetectionEngine.qmd) and its [report](reference/DetectionEngine.report.qmd) |
| not train at all, and use published weights | [`available_weights`](reference/available_weights.qmd) |
| split data without a patient on both sides | [`split_samples`](reference/split_samples.qmd), [`split_dataset`](reference/split_dataset.qmd) |

## What the reference is generated from

The pages under **Reference** come from the docstrings through
[quartodoc](https://machow.github.io/quartodoc/), so they cannot describe a function this
package does not have. The `>>>` examples in them are run by `pytest --doctest-modules`,
which means the site cannot publish an example that does not work - five claims written
into `Args:` and `Returns:` were false when they were first written, and the doctests
caught every one.

The configuration fields are documented on the models themselves, so the YAML reference and
the validation messages say the same thing because they are the same text.
